scope_intro: An automated security assessment of {target} was carried out using the following tools. Each one analyses a different layer of the target; their results are chained to widen coverage.
scope_tool_nmap: Nmap — port and service discovery; identifies software and versions.
scope_tool_nikto: Nikto — web server checks (headers, exposed files, weak configurations).
scope_tool_wapiti: Wapiti — web application tests (injection, XSS, LFI).
scope_limitations: The assessment reflects the state of the target at execution time. Automated tools may produce false positives and do not replace a manual review.

owasp_impact_injection: Injection vulnerabilities allow unintended commands or queries to run, risking data access or system takeover.
owasp_impact_broken_auth: Authentication flaws allow user impersonation or bypassing of access controls.
owasp_impact_xss: Cross-site scripting allows code execution in other users' browsers and session theft.
owasp_impact_broken_access: Broken access control allows reaching resources or actions the user is not authorised for.
owasp_impact_security_misconfig: Poor security configuration widens the attack surface and exposes internal infrastructure to reconnaissance.
owasp_impact_sensitive_exposure: Sensitive data exposure can be exploited immediately to reach internal systems or customer records.
owasp_impact_outdated_components: Outdated components accumulate known, public vulnerabilities that are easy to exploit.
owasp_impact_logging_monitoring: Lack of logging and monitoring hinders detecting and responding to incidents.
owasp_impact_other: These findings require individual review and context-specific mitigation.
rec_generic: Assess whether this resource or behaviour needs to be exposed and restrict it if it provides no operational value.
rec_header_present: Security header present. Verify its value is restrictive enough for the application context.
rec_header_custom: Custom application header. Review that it does not disclose technology stack information.
rec_x_frame_options: Set 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' (or 'SAMEORIGIN' if self-framing is required) to prevent clickjacking.
rec_x_content_type_options: Add 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' to prevent MIME sniffing.
rec_csp: Implement a restrictive Content Security Policy (no 'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-eval').
rec_cors: Restrict 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' to the specific origins needed; avoid the '*' wildcard.
rec_etag: Configure ETags to exclude the inode number (FileETag MTime Size in Apache).
rec_robots: Review robots.txt entries: they must not be used to hide sensitive paths, since they are public.
rec_http_methods: Disable unneeded HTTP methods (PUT, DELETE, TRACE) in the web server configuration.
rec_interesting_path: Review the discovered path and restrict access if it exposes information or functionality not intended for the public.
rec_directory_listing: Disable directory listing (Options -Indexes in Apache / autoindex off in Nginx).
rec_backup_file: Remove publicly accessible backup or configuration files.
rec_version_disclosure: Hide the server and component version in response headers.
remediation_guide_injection: Use parameterized queries and prepared statements for all database interactions. Apply strict whitelist-based input validation on every entry point. Enforce least privilege on all service and database accounts. Schedule a targeted code review of every data-entry path.
remediation_guide_broken_auth: Replace all default and hardcoded credentials immediately. Enforce strong password policies and implement MFA for privileged accounts. Rotate every exposed secret, API key and certificate found in the audit. Review session management: use HttpOnly, SameSite cookies with short TTL.
remediation_guide_xss: Deploy a strict Content-Security-Policy (CSP) header across all pages. Enable automatic output escaping in all template engines. Validate and sanitise every user-supplied input server-side before rendering.
remediation_guide_broken_access: Implement RBAC enforced server-side on every API request. Apply deny-by-default: explicitly whitelist permitted actions per role. Audit all admin panels and direct-object references found during the scan.
remediation_guide_security_misconfig: Disable all services not required for the application. Harden exposed services using CIS Benchmarks. Close unnecessary ports identified in the nmap scan via firewall rules. Remove debug endpoints, directory listings and verbose errors in production.
remediation_guide_sensitive_exposure: Rotate all secrets, API keys and certificates identified as exposed. Remove backup files, source archives and environment files from web-accessible paths. Enforce TLS 1.2+ for all sensitive data in transit. Review cloud storage policies to ensure no public read access.
remediation_guide_outdated_components: Apply patches for all identified outdated components (72 h for critical CVEs). Subscribe to vendor security advisories and CVE feeds. Establish a monthly patch management cadence for non-critical updates.
remediation_guide_logging_monitoring: Centralise security logs (ELK / Splunk or equivalent). Configure alerts for authentication failures, privilege escalations and anomalous access. Define log retention policies that meet compliance requirements.
remediation_guide_other: Review each finding in the Technical Report and apply vendor-recommended mitigations. Prioritise based on exploitability and potential business impact.
